title: HULK Smash, Commish Crash: Ramon Flattens The Horse is Hea as Alan's New Arrivals Cash In
dek: No Banner only HULK posted the week's top score to bury Sonny, while Team Pillbert's trade haul delivered 35.6 points in a fifth straight win, and every favorite in the league held serve.
body: The 4-1 showdown turned out to be a demolition. Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 134.4 to 102.58, the week's top score by more than 27 points, behind a backfield that simply would not stop. Kenneth Walker III posted 26.9 on a 21.85 projection and Christian McCaffrey added 26.2 on a 19.15 projection, which made them the top two performers in the league and good for 53.1 points combined. The HULK is now 5-1 with 829.4 points, 97.8 ahead of anyone else. Strangely, its title odds still slipped from 55% to 50%, because the team right behind it keeps eating.

For Sonny, the first Sunday after the big trade with Alan went about as badly as the model predicted. James Cook III did his part with 22.8 on an 18.53 projection, but George Pickens scored 10.3 on the bench and Ollie Gordon II put up a zero there, while Bryce Young added 19.84 more from the pine. Meanwhile, the two players he shipped out, Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith, combined for 35.6 in Team Pillbert's lineup. The Horse is Hea falls to 4-2 with 86% playoff odds and an 11% title chance, which is still very much a contender, but no longer one of the two teams setting the pace.

Alan's Team Pillbert beat Randy's The fumblers 107.06 to 85.5 as a 59% favorite, and it was the trade return that did the heavy lifting: Hubbard's 18.6 and Smith's 17 alone outscored the 21.56-point margin. Javonte Williams added 12 against the team that traded him, the matchup Randy had been dreading all week. Team Pillbert has now won five straight, sits at 5-1, and holds the 26% title odds it grabbed with the Sonny deal, up from 16% heading into last week. The guy everyone loves rooting against is not going away quietly.

Randy's afternoon was a study in wrong-place, wrong-time. Derrick Henry managed 4.5 points on a 17.6 projection, the week's second-biggest bust, while Trevor Lawrence threw for 27.34 on the bench, the top bench blunder in the league. Stefon Diggs scored 13.4 on the bench too, a rare decent week that never made it into a lineup. The fumblers have now dropped three straight, sit at 3-3, and their title odds fell from 4% to 2%, with playoff odds at 34%.

Mekhi's Dawgs beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 105.6 to 83.44 as a 64% favorite, and Malik Nabers, last week's waiver addition, paid off right away with 22.5 on a 14.6 projection. Ashton Jeanty chipped in 13.8, enough to cover for Kyren Williams' 8.2 on a 19.17 projection. The timing gods did find Kai one more time, though: a week after Tyler Shough scored -0.16 in his lineup, Shough sat on the bench and threw for 26.96. Zoe never recovered from Bijan Robinson's 6.3 on a 21.34 projection, the week's biggest bust, and the rookie drops to 2-4 with playoff odds down to 5%.

Kaushal's Habibsters held off Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 100.5 to 92.72 as a 70% favorite. Drake Maye, whom Habib re-added this week by dropping Sam Darnold, scored 23.8 on a 20.25 projection, so the quarterback carousel that spun one way in Week 4 finally spun back into a win. JMoney got a breakout from Bhayshul Tuten, 22.7 on an 11.69 projection, plus 20.9 from Isaiah Likely, but Emeka Egbuka scored 14.3 on the bench while Denzel Boston started and scored 2. That 12.3-point gap is bigger than the 7.78-point margin, which means the lineup decision may have been the difference. Counting or not Counting GV is 1-5 with playoff odds at 0%.

The standings now have a clear top tier: the HULK and Team Pillbert at 5-1, with 100% and 99% playoff odds, then The Horse is Hea at 4-2. The fourth seed is where things get weird. The fumblers hold it at 3-3, but Habibsters have 677.9 points to Randy's 643.8, and the model gives the 2-4 Habibsters better playoff odds, 41% to 34%, with Dawgs right there at 36%. On the wire, Alan was busy again, adding Tank Dell, Brenton Strange, Dameon Pierce, and Josh Jacobs, and cutting Tyreek Hill and Odell Beckham Jr. Kaushal picked up Woody Marks and dropped him within the week for Tony Pollard, and grabbed Juwan Johnson for Rome Odunze right after Sonny cut Johnson for Pat Freiermuth. The commish also dropped Jalen Hurts, added Jameson Williams, and swapped the Bears D/ST for the 49ers D/ST, a Chicago guy cutting the Bears defense from Boston. Zoe dropped Lamar Jackson and added Jordan Love for Blake Corum, and Randy cut kicker Brandon Aubrey and swapped the Raiders D/ST for the Rams D/ST.

Week 7 has stakes all over the board. The fumblers and The Horse is Hea meet with Randy trying to snap a three-game skid and Sonny trying to stay a clear step ahead of the fourth-seed scramble. Dawgs and Habibsters, both 2-4 and both coming off wins, play what is essentially a playoff elimination game in October. Zoe gets Alan's five-game streak, and the HULK hosts Jordan, who needs something close to a miracle and a better read on his receivers.

social.author: HULK Nation
social.text: Walker 26.9. McCaffrey 26.2. 134.4 on the board. Commish came in with title dreams and left with a box score. 829.4 points and counting.

social.author: Pillbert Fan Club
social.text: Five straight. Hubbard 18.6, Smith 17, Javonte 12 against his old team. The trade debut went exactly how we drew it up. Zoe, you're next.

social.author: Fumblers Fan Forum
social.text: Henry 4.5. Lawrence 27.34 on the bench. Diggs 13.4 on the bench. Three straight losses. We are still the four seed and we will be holding onto that very tightly.

social.author: Dawgs Insider
social.text: Sources confirm Tyler Shough has now scored -0.16 as a starter and 26.96 as a backup in back-to-back weeks. Sources also confirm Dawgs won anyway. Nabers 22.5, thanks for coming.

social.author: Habibsters Hype
social.text: Maye back on the roster, Maye drops 23.8, W in the books. 677.9 points, 41% playoff odds, better than the team sitting in fourth. Two-time champs don't stay buried.

social.author: The Fantasy Spreadsheet
social.text: Every favorite won this week. Fun fact: the 2-4 Habibsters (41%) and 2-4 Dawgs (36%) both have better playoff odds than the 3-3 fumblers (34%). The record says one thing. The points say another.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN Stans
social.text: Bijan 6.3 on a 21.34 projection. Rough one. New QB on the roster, Team Pillbert on deck, and nobody's playing for 5% on purpose. Let's swing.

social.author: GV Number Crunchers
social.text: Tuten 22.7 on an 11.69 projection, Likely 20.9, lost by 7.78. Egbuka's 14.3 on the bench is not something we are discussing tonight.

social.author: BFL Waiver Watch
social.text: Sonny cut Juwan Johnson for Freiermuth. Kaushal picked up Juwan Johnson the same week. Kaushal also added and dropped Woody Marks before the paint dried. The wire never sleeps.

trade_watch.take: Week one went exactly the way the odds said it would: Hubbard and Smith combined for 35.6 in Team Pillbert's win, while Pickens (10.3) and Gordon (0) both sat on Sonny's bench in a loss to the HULK. Alan's paper win is now a scoreboard win too.

Javonte Williams got his revenge game and put up 12 in a win over the team that traded him, bringing his total to 54 in Alan's lineup. Diggs finally had a decent week with 13.4, but it came on Randy's bench, and the lineup gap is now 54 to 6.

Mekhi keeps widening this one: Jeanty's 13.8 and Adams' 5.4 helped Dawgs win, and the pair now has 48 lineup points against Jefferson's 15.8. Jefferson scored zero for Alan this week and didn't start, so the gap went from 13 to 32.2.

Isaiah Likely is still carrying Jordan's side with 20.9 and 47.8 lineup points, but the rest of the return is a lineup puzzle: Egbuka has 28.5 points and zero of them in a lineup, including 14.3 on the bench in a 7.78-point loss. Alan got nothing from Jeanty, so this is still JMoney's deal, just one he keeps leaving points on.

bios.1: Sonny's crew got run over by the HULK and watched its new arrivals, Pickens and Gordon, sit on the bench while the players it traded starred elsewhere. At 4-2 with 86% playoff odds, the defending champ is safe for now but has slid to an 11% title shot. Randy's slumping fumblers are next.
bios.2: Randy has lost three straight and was undone by Derrick Henry's 4.5 points and Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 on the bench. The fumblers still hold the fourth seed at 3-3, but two 2-4 teams have better playoff odds. A date with the commissioner decides which way this goes.
bios.3: Jordan got breakout games from Bhayshul Tuten and Isaiah Likely and still lost by 7.78, with Emeka Egbuka's 14.3 stuck on the bench. At 1-5 with 0% playoff odds, the season is about pride now. The HULK is next, which is the toughest possible test for it.
bios.4: Alan has won five straight, and the Hubbard-and-Smith trade paid off on day one with 35.6 points in a win over Randy. At 5-1 with a 26% title chance, Team Pillbert is the clear second favorite, and the transaction log is still spinning. Zoe gets the next crack at the streak.
bios.5: Mekhi's waiver work keeps paying off, with Malik Nabers scoring 22.5 in a win over Zoe and the Adams-Jeanty trade continuing to deliver. The only catch was Tyler Shough's 26.96 on the bench. At 2-4 with 36% playoff odds, Dawgs face Habibsters in a battle for the fourth-seed chase.
bios.6: Kaushal is 2-4 but has scored 677.9 points, more than the team in fourth place, and the model has noticed, giving him 41% playoff odds. Drake Maye came back to the roster and delivered 23.8 in a win. The Dawgs game next week is a must-win in October.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 5-1 with 829.4 points, nearly 100 more than anyone else, and just dropped the week's top score on the commissioner. Walker and McCaffrey are rolling, playoff odds are locked at 100%, and the only thing slowing the title odds is Team Pillbert's streak. Jordan is up next.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season hit a bump with a second straight loss, as Bijan Robinson managed just 6.3 against Dawgs. At 2-4 with 5% playoff odds, she has reshuffled at quarterback, dropping Lamar Jackson for Jordan Love. Taking down Alan's five-game streak would be a big statement.
